dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Such honest passion... How can it not be called beauty?

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Oh, I was just reliving last night's performance.

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: You see, traditional Snezhnayan opera tends to focus on grand tragedies — filling emotional gaps with overly elaborate lyrics...

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: But the performances by Miss Odette and Lady Vodyanitsa discard all that unnecessary excess. Elegant. Truly, what elegance!

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Take Miss Odette's footwork, for example — it is less "dance" than it is "martial form." You follow my meaning, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Farewell. I do hope that one day, you too will come to appreciate the discipline and beauty of this art form.

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: You have good taste, my friend! Miss Odette's choreography always carries a sense of martial restraint.

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Many performers, when expressing intense emotion, tend to fall into chaotic physical excess... but she is different.

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Some of my fellow critics — though forgive my bluntness, they truly understand nothing — love to compare her with her mother and analyze the similarities between their styles...

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: But from a truly professional standpoint, Madame Violetta's style leans toward absolute classical restraint, whereas Miss Odette....

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: Ah, never mind. True art should be felt, not explained. What words cannot convey should simply remain in silence!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I don't understand what you're talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Pisemsky
dialogues.text: It's alright. True art should be felt, not explained. What words cannot convey should simply remain in silence!
